name: Eldgjá volcanic eruption in Iceland
summary: One of the largest basaltic flood-lava eruptions of the past two millennia. Eldgjá's tephra and sulphate aerosols depress Northern Hemisphere temperatures for several years; chronicles from Ireland to China record unusually dim, reddish skies in 939–940.

_quarry.structural_significance: Recent ice-core and dendrochronological work links the eruption to crop failures across Europe and the Mediterranean in the early 940s; the timing roughly coincides with the formal Christianisation of Iceland (1000) and may have influenced the religious-cultural shift.
